title: CPTAC-Brain, Head and Neck, Kidney, Lung, Pancreas, Uterus
summary:
CPTAC-3 is the genomic half of a cohort whose proteomic half lives in a different repository. That split is the single most important practical fact about it: the GDC record carries exome on 1,844 cases, whole genome on 1,827, RNA sequencing on 1,824 and methylation on 1,817, while proteome, phosphoproteome and the scarcer modification layers are distributed through the Proteomic Data Commons under different study identifiers.
Its clinical annotation is unusually strong for a multi-cancer cohort. Vital status is informative for 95.8%, progression or recurrence for 77.9%, and last known disease status for 77.2% - which makes recurrence-based endpoints genuinely available, not just nominally present.
one_liner: 1,866 tumors across six cancer types with genomics in the GDC and proteomics in the PDC - the largest prospectively collected proteogenomic cohort, with recurrence recorded for 78% of cases.

useful_for.question: Which genomic alterations have consequences at the protein level, and which do not?
useful_for.rationale: This is the question CPTAC exists to answer, and it needs both halves joined. Genomics on over 1,800 cases here pairs with proteomic studies in the PDC on the same participants, allowing copy number and mutation effects to be traced to protein and phosphosite abundance.
useful_for.statistical_note: The proteomic layers cover subsets of the cohort organized by cancer type, so the joined analysis is substantially smaller than 1,866 and varies by tumor type. Build the intersection first.

evidence.note: Written by a named reviewer after reading the source documentation and the measured field coverage. Not machine-generated.

useful_for.question: What molecular features predict recurrence across cancer types?
useful_for.rationale: Progression or recurrence is informative for 77.9% of 1,866 cases with a median follow-up of 22.8 months - unusual completeness for a recurrence endpoint, and the basis for a genuinely pan-cancer recurrence analysis.
useful_for.statistical_note: Pan-cancer recurrence pooling mixes very different natural histories; stratify by tumor type and treat the pooled estimate as secondary.

useful_for.question: Do proteogenomic subtypes cut across tissue of origin?
useful_for.rationale: Six cancer types collected prospectively under a common protocol make cross-tissue subtype comparison less confounded by collection differences than a retrospective pan-cancer assembly.

limitations.statement: The proteomic data that define this cohort's purpose are not in this record. They are distributed through the Proteomic Data Commons as separate per-fraction studies with their own identifiers, and joining them is the analyst's responsibility.
limitations.mitigation: Retrieve the corresponding PDC studies and join on case identifier. Budget real time for this; it is the most common place CPTAC reuse stalls.

limitations.mitigation: 22 cases cannot support conclusions about Black patients. The Asian subgroup is large enough for some comparisons but is confounded with collection site.
